title: graphrefly-rs DeferredCtx holds a STRONG Core (Rc<RefCell<NodeInner>>): an async fn that stashes ctx.defer() and never emits (abandoned/cancelled work, a never-resolving backend) pins the node's NodeInner — and thus its fn slot (blocking the B32 unregister), its captured upstream Cores, and its dep_unsubs subscriptions — alive until the DeferredCtx drops. title: RxJS-7 time-operator complete-edge reference (context7-verified /reactivex/rxjs 7.8.2, 2026-05-30) -- pins the per-operator source-COMPLETE behavior so it is settled BEFORE implementation, NOT left to discover. R-terminals and reference/kernel/kernel.mjs agree on an INVALIDATE and a dependency's ERROR in one wave: the rule says an INVALIDATE that reached the node before the ERROR takes effect first, and the reference applies an INVALIDATE of any input in that wave whatever their order.

A kernel rule says in which order a node under the auto INVALIDATE policy sends, when one input's INVALIDATE and another input's DATA come in one wave; the reference kernel sends the retraction first whatever their order, and R-invalidation speaks of one input only.

The rules and reference/kernel/kernel.mjs agree on a dependency given twice: the kernel takes it when a node is created and refuses it at a rewire or a replace, also for a list that already holds one.

The cycle check of a replace covers the dependencies a restored node holds for its first lifetime: before that node's first activation the reference accepts a replace that makes the two depend on each other, which it refuses on a live graph.

A kernel rule says in which order requests made by different nodes in one wave are carried out, and what a checkpoint keeps of it; R-request-order says requests run in the order they were made, the reference makes them in the order nodes ran, which follows the order sinks subscribed and the order of a batch's writes, and a restored graph has no subscribers until the host subscribes again.

R-checkpoint, or a rule it cites, says what a restore does with a node whose declared dependencies repeat one node: reference/modules/checkpoint.mjs refuses a repeated dependency of the saved lifetime and takes a repeated declared one, which a later replace then cannot repair.

R-node says whether the definition a read returns is the host's to change: the reference returns the stored recipe itself, so an edit of its configuration changes what a capture writes and not what the live node does, and the two then disagree after a restore.

A kernel rule says what a dependent is given, and what it may go on counting, when one of its dependencies is replaced by a new instance of the same id while the dependent stays active: the reference kernel keeps nothing of the old instance, its terminal included, for a node under the auto COMPLETE policy, and gives a function no sign of the replacement, so a node that records a dependency's COMPLETE in its private state goes on counting it.

The user has decided whether R-checkpoint's comparison by held value stands as it is: a restored node does not run for a dependency that sent again a value equal to the one the node had received, which a node that stayed live takes for an occurrence.

Each point is settled by the user as a clarification of what is already meant or as a choice, and a rule revision goes through spec-amend with its scenario and model obligations before any runtime follows.
